description: A Gantt chart for project schedules in Microsoft Power BI, with honest parent rows, dependencies, baselines and earned value. Who it's for Project managers and PMOs reporting schedules in Power BI. Portfolio analysts whose task data already sits in a Power BI model. The problem it solves Parent rows are averaged, so a two-day task counts as much as a two-month one. Critical path and float need extra columns calculated somewhere else. Baseline slip is eyeballed, and earned value is often rebuilt outside Power BI. What you get Hierarchy: WBS numbers and a duration-weighted rollup; expand and collapse survive refresh and are saved with the report. Timeline: zoom from years to seconds, or click the header to drill in. Zooming never filters the report. Calendar: weekends, days off, holidays, fiscal years and ISO weeks. Dependencies: all four link types with lead and lag, plus a computed critical path and float. Baselines: up to three, with a finish-variance column in days. KPI band: plot any measure on the same time axis as the tasks. Earned value: S-curve, SPI, CPI and a DCMA 14-point schedule assessment, with any point your data can't answer marked not assessable. Insights: progress, slippage and the longest chain in plain sentences. Also: colour rules, resource lanes, workload histogram, search, annotations, table view with export, chart text in ten languages (the settings panel…
